title: A Horizon-Specific Attribute-Conditioned Neural Network for Estimating Health-State Transition Probabilities in Irregular Longitudinal Data: The LANTERN Framework
abstract: arXiv:2606.13880v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Accurate estimation of health-state transition probabilities is essential for long-term care insurance modeling. Conventional actuarial multi-state models provide an interpretable framework but may be restrictive in capturing nonlinear relationships and accumulated health histories from irregular longitudinal observations. This paper proposes LANTERN, a history-dependent neural framework that integrates recurrent health representations, elapsed observation time, and adaptive demographic and socioeconomic attribute conditioning to estimate horizon-specific transition probabilities among Healthy, Mild disability, Severe disability, and Death states. Using longitudinal Health and Retirement Study data, we evaluate our model against a recurrent neural network, multinomial logistic regression, gradient-boosted trees, and an actuarial continuous-time Markov chain across one-, two-, and three-year forecast horizons. translated_title: 一种针对特定预测期、基于属性条件化的神经网络，用于在不规则纵向数据中估计健康状态转移概率：LANTERN 框架
translated_abstract: 准确估计健康状态转移概率对于长期护理保险建模至关重要。传统的精算多状态模型提供了可解释的框架，但在捕捉非线性关系以及从不规则纵向观测中积累的健康历史方面可能存在局限。本文提出 LANTERN，这是一个依赖历史的神经框架，它整合了循环健康状态表示、观测间隔时间，以及自适应的人口统计与社会经济属性条件化，用于估计健康、轻度失能、重度失能和死亡四种状态之间的特定预测期转移概率。利用健康与退休研究（Health and Retirement Study）的纵向数据，我们在一年、两年和三年的预测期上，将所提出的模型与循环神经网络、多项逻辑回归、梯度提升树以及精算连续时间马尔可夫链进行了对比评估。在主要的两年预测期上……
tldr: 本文提出 LANTERN 框架，通过整合循环健康表示、观测间隔时间与自适应的人口社会经济属性条件化，从不规则纵向数据中估计特定预测期的健康状态转移概率，为长期护理保险建模提供了超越传统精算多状态模型的新方法。
en_tdlr: LANTERN is a history-dependent neural framework that integrates recurrent health representations, elapsed observation time, and adaptive demographic and socioeconomic attribute conditioning to estimate horizon-specific health-state transition probabilities from irregular longitudinal data, offering a novel approach for long-term care insurance modeling beyond conventional actuarial multi-state models.
